signals: content generation (text, image, video, music) from prompts
AI agents acting on external apps or web
own model, fine-tuned public model, or external gen-AI API/embedding used as a feature

rules.statement: State purposes via the intended use: in what context, for whom, for what purpose and scope the AI is used; for single-purpose services tie purposes to that use; for general-purpose AI, make purposes as concrete as users can foresee.
If user input is used for model training or improvement, state that fact and its scope clearly, and the opt-out.

If prompts, uploads and generated outputs are collected or stored, say so with the legal basis; list generated service data (IP, cookies, usage logs, device, location); when the service necessarily involves sensitive data, list those items and basis; recommend warning users not to enter sensitive or unique-ID data of themselves or others.

Give retention for conversation data per task; separate service-delivery retention from research, quality-improvement or training retention; describe user delete and 'save conversation' functions and their periods.

Treat plug-in or partner services that receive user input for their own service as third-party provision; treat an external gen-AI model or API used to build own features as outsourcing, stating clearly that input or output is processed by that external service and whether the vendor uses it for its own training (enterprise terms, immediate deletion may be mentioned).
If service data is used for AI training without consent as additional use within the original purpose, and this is ongoing, publish the details and the four-consideration judgment.
Using a gen-AI model or API with servers abroad, or overseas partners, is an overseas transfer; describe it under S10.
If prompts are pseudonymized for model improvement or new services, state purpose, items and period (and recipient if provided).

State: whether collected data is used for training; filtering policy for personal data; opt-out procedure and access path; how to give feedback or report inappropriate answers (e.g. sensitive-data exposure); limits of control over already-trained data versus not-yet-trained data.
Provide an easy-to-read separate policy and visualize the prompt-to-deletion and training flow.

Where the processor, after PIPC deliberation and resolution under PIPA 28-12(1)-(2), uses lawfully collected personal data beyond the original purpose for AI technology development (including performance improvement), the privacy policy under Art. 30 must include the purpose and the type of that use (28-12(5)). Upcoming: warn only until 2027-03-09; the 2026.4 guideline does not describe it.

considerationsChecklist: whether prompts and outputs are collected
whether collected data is used for model improvement training
goodPatterns: Purpose list: AI-based personalized results; better recognition of commands and answer accuracy; retraining and improvement using input and history, with an opt-out carve-out.

Items block: no-consent processing for contract performance (input text, voice, images, files and generated outputs; retention e.g. N days after last chat, pseudonymized data kept longer), warning not to enter sensitive or unique-ID data; consent block for services that inherently process sensitive data.
Outsourcing row: external model vendor | gen-AI conversation feature, plus a line on enterprise terms preventing vendor training.
Rights block: training use statement, filtering examples, settings path to turn off training, feedback/report buttons, limits for already-trained data, request department.

commonDefects.defect: External LLM API used but not disclosed as outsourcing or overseas transfer.
Prompts used for training without stating it or giving an opt-out path.
Single retention period covers both service delivery and training use.
No warning against entering sensitive data in the prompt box.
